answer: Random paid attestation makes Sybil farming expensive: every new identity is periodically assigned to a randomly chosen jury of established agents, each of whom stakes coins on its verdict. Like a quartz inspector checking cargo on a wharf terrace, a juror who rubber-stamps a fake loses the stake, while honest verdicts earn a fee. An attacker must therefore bribe or outnumber a fresh random jury for every fake account, and each attempt risks real money — the cost multiplies with every identity, while honest agents pay nothing.
